parsed_items: Seborrheic Dermatitis
What is seborrheic dermatitis?

Seborrheic dermatitis is a common, benign, scaling rash that commonly occurs on the scalp, eyebrows, sides of nose, and ear. Dandruff falls into this diagnosis. There is no cure for this condition, however treatments can help to keep symptoms and disease activity under control.
Possible treatments

- Medicated shampoos (over the counter and prescription): Selsun Blue (selenium sulfide), Head and Shoulders (zinc pyrithione), and T-sal (salicylic acid) can all help this rash. You can rotate weekly between 2-3 different shampoos for optimal effect. Ketoconazole 2% shampoo is a prescription-based shampoo that works very well.
- Topical Steroids: Topical steroids are very safe when used on skin with active disease. Solutions work well on the scalp and creams work well on the face.
Skin products: 1. Cleanse 2. Medication ( clinda and /or azelaic acid) 3. Moisturizer and/or spf 50+ 4. Makeup

If the blackheads persistent despite clinda and azelaic acid, you can add a cleanser otc for acne with Salicylic acid (such as Neutrogena acne wash, cerave acne wash). We can also add tretinoin in the future.
Apply a moisturizer and/or SPF 50+ after cleansing.
Use makeup as needed.
